explanation: In a perfectly inelastic collision the carts STICK and move off as one combined lump at the common velocity vf. Momentum still has to balance, so vf is just the mass-weighted average of the incoming speeds — set the masses and speeds and watch p (kg·m/s) read the same before and after. Kinetic energy, however, does NOT survive: the readout shows KE drop, with the lost energy going into heat and deformation when they crunch together.
bullets: They stick, so both share one velocity vf = total momentum / total mass.
Momentum is conserved; the p readout is identical before and after.
Kinetic energy is LOST (to heat/deformation) — KE_after < KE_before.
